description: Evaluate an expression in a running extension context. Start the session with allowEval:true (extension_dev), which writes a 0600 session token; without that token every route of this tool, the debug port included, answers eval-disabled. Context defaults to 'background', except on a Chromium MV3 session (the default template) where it defaults to 'page', the active tab; pass context:'background' to evaluate in the service worker, which on Chromium goes over the debug port. Debug-port evaluates run with a user gesture, so gesture-gated APIs (permissions.request, sidePanel.open) can succeed here and still fail when the extension's own code calls them. For content and page, pass `url` to pick the tab, or omit both `url` and `tab` for the active tab; a numeric `tab` only disambiguates. Extension surfaces (popup, options, sidebar, devtools) and override pages (newtab, history, bookmarks) need no tab id but must already be open: open one with extension_open first, because a closed one returns an explicit error. On a Chromium MV3 session those pages, and context:'page' with a chrome-extension:// url, evaluate over CDP, the inspector path the extension page CSP does not govern; elsewhere they evaluate over the in-bundle relay. On Firefox a document whose content security policy forbids eval (the extension's own pages, or a site's) is evaluated over the debugger protocol instead, which takes one expression; a page inside the extension that is no declared surface (pages/*) is reached the same way by context:'page' and its moz-extension:// url once a tab shows it. An extension_start session's pages carry no relay, so there a surface shown in a tab (options) and an extension page url are evaluated over the debugger protocol too; a surface in its own window (popup) is not reachable on that session, and the answer says so instead of reporting a missing target. Naming a tab the browser refuses to script (page-not-scriptable, extension-page-unreachable) needs Extension.js 4.1.34, not yet released; on 4.1.33 such a refusal still answers as a missing target, with the hint that the tab could not be reached. A returned promise is awaited: over CDP and the Firefox debugger protocol, in a Firefox background, and in tabs (page or content through the in-tab executor) and relay surfaces, where this tool polls until it settles or timeout passes. The one exception is Firefox MV2 without the scripting API, where the expression runs through tabs.executeScript and must return a synchronous value. A value that cannot be cloned (a DOM node, a function) comes back as its string form, or as a not-cloneable error where the browser itself refuses to copy it. To wait for a condition that is still settling (a model loading, an element appearing), pass until: {} (or {timeoutMs, intervalMs}) and the eval repeats until its value is truthy, answering that value, or the last one on timeout. Pass `targetId` (the target.targetId extension_open answers, or one from extension_dom_snapshot listTargets:true) to evaluate in that exact page over the debug port, the CDP target on Chromium or the tab on Firefox; context, url and tab are then ignored. A url that matches several tabs showing the same page evaluates in the most recently active one and warns with the others' targetIds. Call extension_dom_snapshot with listTabs:true to enumerate {tabId, url, title}.

browser.description: Session browser; defaults to this project's live session. Required when the project runs sessions for more than one browser: the call is refused with the list rather than picking one.

context.description: Where to evaluate. Default background, except Chromium MV3 sessions default to page (the active tab).

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate in the target context

projectPath.description: Extension project root (needs a live dev session)

tab.description: Numeric chrome.tabs id, only to disambiguate when several tabs match.

targetId.description: Pick one open page directly by its targetId: the target.targetId extension_open answers, or a targetId from extension_dom_snapshot listTargets: true (a CDP target id on Chromium, the tab's browserId on Firefox). When given, `url` is ignored. A target that is gone is refused with E_TARGET_NOT_FOUND, naming the live ones.

timeout.description: Command timeout in ms. When omitted, the default depends on the route: 30000 through the dev session's control channel, 10000 over the Firefox debugger protocol, and 15000 per command over the Chromium debug port.

until.description: Repeat the eval until it returns a truthy value, for a condition that is still settling (a model loading, an element appearing), instead of answering the first reading. Pass {} for the defaults. Answers status "condition-met" with value.result (the truthy value) and value.polls, or status "timeout" (E_WAIT_TIMEOUT) with value.lastResult, the last value read. A refusal polling cannot change (eval disabled, no such surface, an ended Safari session) answers at once. Works on Chromium, Firefox and Safari sessions. Never sleep or tail the session log in a shell to wait.

intervalMs.description: Pause between evals. Default 500, clamped to 100-10000.

timeoutMs.description: Budget for the whole wait. Default 30000, clamped to 1000-50000 so one call stays under the client's 60s request timeout. On timeout, call again to keep waiting.

url.description: content/page: pick the tab by url (match pattern, then substring). Preferred over `tab`.

name: extension_eval
